core_step: List files in /root/papers/all to discover the files to categorize
why_essential: You must know which files exist and how many there are before you can categorize or move them

core_step: Extract first-page text from each PDF using pdftotext to determine each paper's subject
why_essential: Reading the first page/title of each PDF gives the subject/topic needed to assign the file to the correct subject folder
evidence: "pdftotext -l 1 \"$f\" - 2>/dev/null | head -20"" and output showing titles such as "Lower ground state ... trapped ion system"

core_step: Extract contents of DOCX and PPTX by opening them as zip archives and reading XML to determine their topics
why_essential: DOCX/PPTX cannot be parsed by pdftotext; reading their internal XML (via zipfile) reveals titles/slide text needed for correct categorization
evidence: "with zipfile.ZipFile('/root/papers/all/paper_file_1.docx'...)" -> "Temporally multiplexed ion-photon quantum interface"; "DAMOP PRESENTATION - ALL SLIDE TITLES"

core_step: Create the five target folders: LLM, trapped_ion_and_qc, black_hole, DNA, music_history
why_essential: Folders must exist as destinations before files can be moved into the appropriate subject directories

core_step: Move each file into its determined subject folder using mv
why_essential: Physically relocating files into the subject folders is the required state change that completes the organization task
evidence: "mv 2306.08568v2.pdf 2308.16149v2.pdf ..." and multiple subsequent mv commands with no output (completed)

core_step: Verify the organization by counting files in each subject folder
why_essential: A final verification ensures all files were moved and no files remain unassigned
evidence: "for dir in LLM trapped_ion_and_qc black_hole DNA music_history; do count=$(ls /root/papers/$dir/ | wc -l); ..." -> "LLM: 20 files ..." and totals summing to all files
